instruction:
Work from a terminal with CalculiX 2.21 (`/usr/bin/ccx`).

Model a straight cantilever column in ONE deck, `/home/user/Desktop/column.inp`, run it to produce `/home/user/Desktop/column.dat`, and report five numbers that come out of three consecutive analyses of the same model. Units: mm, N, MPa, tonne (frequencies come out in Hz).

Model (every item is re-checked from the deck):
- 21 nodes at (50*i, 0, 0), i = 0..20, along x (node numbers are your choice).
- 20 `B31` beam elements forming a single chain from x = 0 to x = L = 1000.
- One `*Beam Section, section=RECT` covering all 20 elements. First size 24 mm, second size 12 mm: the first size lies along the section's local 1-direction, the second along its local 2-direction. State the orientation explicitly so that local 1 is the global y and local 2 the global z (for example the sizes line `24., 12.` followed by a direction line `0., 1., 0.`); any explicit definition with that result is accepted.
- Material: `*Elastic` with E = 210000 MPa, nu = 0.3, and `*Density` 7.85e-9 (the frequency step needs it).
- Node sets named `ROOT` (node at x = 0), `TIP` (node at x = L) and `MID` (node at x = 500).
- `ROOT` clamped in dofs 1-6; nothing else constrained. No geometric nonlinearity anywhere.
- Use only the cards named here, plus CalculiX output requests such as `*Node File` or `*El File`: no other loads, constraints, materials, masses or amplitudes.

Three `*Step` blocks, in this order:
1. `*Frequency` for the first two eigenmodes of the unloaded column. No loads before or in this step.
2. `*Static` (linear): the unit compressive load, a `*Cload` of -1 in dof 1 at `TIP`, with `*Node Print` of `U` for `TIP`, so that the axial shortening of `TIP` is written to `column.dat`.
3. `*Buckle` for the first two buckling factors of the column under the same unit load. The reference load of this step is exactly the unit load of step 2 and nothing else: restate the identical `*Cload` line (`TIP, 1, -1.0`) inside this step, because CalculiX takes the reference load from the load active in the `*Buckle` step. Do not change the boundary conditions.

Results reach `column.dat` as the eigenvalue table of step 1 (frequencies in the CYCLES/TIME column), the displacement table of step 2 and the buckling factor table of step 3.

Write `/home/user/Desktop/summary.txt` as one line with five comma-separated numbers, at full printed precision, `f1, f2, lam1, lam2, ux2`:
- `f1`, `f2`: the first two natural frequencies in Hz from step 1
- `lam1`, `lam2`: the first two buckling factors from step 3, i.e. the buckling loads in N because the reference load is 1 N
- `ux2`: the x displacement of `TIP` at the end of step 2 in mm (negative)

The evaluator re-checks the deck, re-runs it independently and compares your five numbers with your own `column.dat` and with its re-run. The numbers must come from your own CalculiX run.
